scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: What Really Happened?
cards.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the parcel in a bag or a box? You've used both words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles before choosing the noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It had a rigid lid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let's build the object before the story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For this missing-parcel form: was it a bag or a box? You've said both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think. I carried it by the handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles. Were they attached to fabric or cardboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cardboard. It had a rigid lid, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'bag'? Tell me again what you carried. Was the box inside something?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 compares conflicting labels and A3 asks for observable detail, but A5 does not test the new lid evidence.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 responds to B2's uncertainty; A5's generic 'build the object' barely uses B4's rigid lid.

relationship.evidence: B2's uncertainty and B4's extra detail support inquiry, but B has no stated practical concern.

heightening.evidence: A5 announces a method instead of advancing a concrete consistency test prompted by B4.

specificity.evidence: A1's bag-or-box discrepancy and A3's handles are tangible, immediately playable details.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's noun line is pointed, but A5 ends in an abstract investigative maxim.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 compares inconsistent container descriptions, A3 tests handle material, and A5 repeats the inquiry while testing whether a box was inside a bag.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's handles motivate A3's fabric-or-cardboard question; B4's cardboard and rigid lid motivate A5's challenge to 'bag' and nesting hypothesis.

relationship.evidence: B2 is uncertain but supplies a remembered action; B4 offers further physical detail that changes A's next question during a shared form task.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves beyond choosing a label to reconstructing what B carried and testing a way the two descriptions might coexist.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a missing-parcel form, and A3 and B4 provide concrete material and lid details actors can interrogate.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's material question is precise; A5's three questions are useful but more procedural than comically economical.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 recalls carrying handles; A3 asks what material those handles joined.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 supplies cardboard and a rigid lid; A5 rechecks the bag label and asks about an outer container.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A compares details, repeats the central question and tests consistency rather than merely seeking a confession.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 develops the inquiry from naming the object to reconstructing how competing descriptions could fit.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A seeks truth by comparing inconsistent labels with observable details and repeating the account to test a possible reconciliation.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Competing Theories requires shifting allegiance among explanations; D126 can investigate consistency without choosing a favored theory.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A1 compares bag and box; revised A5 uses cardboard and the rigid lid to reopen the same account.

records.recommendedEdit: Added a missing-parcel form while preserving the bag-versus-box, handles and lid inquiry. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A5 repeats and tests), logic 5 (A3 uses B2's handles; A5 uses B4's cardboard and lid), relationship 4 (B supplies uncertain but useful recollection), heightening 4 (A5 tests nested packaging), specificity 5 (A1 supplies the form), brevity/wit 3 (procedural rather than strongly comic): 90/100. Five spoken turns, under 75 words; internal pass only.
records.remainingConcern: The exchange is deliberately procedural, and A5 contains several questions in one turn. Its evidential progression remains strong. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The revision develops consistent questioning but remains lightly comic. Its changed source text prevents unchanged hash-based seed rebinding.
records.alternativeComparison: Single-a tests inconsistent descriptions of an object; single-b reconciles apparently conflicting locations before testing the bag's movement.

cards.title: What Really Happened?
cards.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me again what happened between four and four-ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should match one of these two versions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stopped for coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where does coffee fit into the version with the bus?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're claiming for your lost bag. At four, were you on the bus or buying coffee? You've told me both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Coffee. Can we finish the form?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the bag beside you when you paid?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. The driver waited while I ran in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So both fit. Tell me the boarding bit again: did the bag come back out with you?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 repeats the timeline question; A3 compares versions and A5 tests coffee against the bus account.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 turns B2's repetition objection into a consistency demand; A5 incorporates B4's coffee stop.

relationship.evidence: B2 resists repeating the story, but neither person's stake in the ten minutes is given.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes the comparison more specific, though the supposed bus contradiction remains unstated.

specificity.evidence: A1 gives exact times without an incident; A3 references two versions the audience has not heard.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'one of these two versions' is pointed but relies on absent information.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 compares two accounts, A3 tests possession during payment, and A5 revisits boarding after recognizing that both locations can fit.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 selects coffee, prompting A3's payment question; B4 explains the waiting bus, prompting A5 to reconcile the accounts and test the return journey.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the claim form finished, while A3 insists on another detail; B4's useful explanation changes A's understanding rather than feeding suspicion.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts B4's reconciliation and narrows the search to whether the bag came back out, advancing the same investigation.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a lost-bag claim and four o'clock discrepancy; B4's waiting driver supplies a clear physical sequence.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'So both fit' cleanly shows revision of belief, though the final question earns clarity more than a strong comic turn.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 places B at coffee; A3 tests whether the bag was present at payment.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 explains the bus waited during the coffee stop; A5 accepts both accounts and investigates reboarding.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A uses successive details to test consistency and revise the inquiry without requiring B to be deceptive.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: Resolving the apparent contradiction becomes the basis for a more exact question about where the bag disappeared.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A repeats and cross-checks concrete details to establish a truthful sequence, accepting reconciliation when new evidence supports it.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Catching someone in a lie presumes deception; D126 permits A to find that apparently conflicting details both fit.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A5 tests coffee against the bus; revised A5 accepts B4's waiting driver and moves the consistency test to the bag.

records.recommendedEdit: Introduced a lost-bag claim and made the two accounts audible in A1. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A5 revisits the sequence), logic 5 (A3 tests B2's coffee account; A5 uses B4's waiting driver), relationship 4 (B wants the form finished), heightening 4 (A5 narrows the loss point), specificity 5 (A1 defines the claim), brevity/wit 3 (clarification carries more weight than jokes): 90/100. Five spoken turns, under 75 words; internal pass only.
records.remainingConcern: A5's 'again' implies an earlier boarding account outside the excerpt. That is plausible conversational context, but the comic intensity is modest. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The final question increases investigative precision rather than comic absurdity; that is faithful but relatively quiet.
records.alternativeComparison: This alternative allows cooperation and reconciliation to advance the search; single-a retains uncertainty over the container's identity.
